Implement a runtime instance registry for Storybook that writes a JSON file to disk whenever a Storybook server starts. This will allow external tools to discover running instances and determine if an AI integration addon is available. Ensure the system supports cleaning up the record when the instance stops and provide a higher-level function to manage the full lifecycle.

*   Implement `getMcpMetadataFromMainConfig` in `code/core/src/core-server/utils/runtime-instance-registry.ts`.
    *   Return `{ status: 'not-installed' }` if `@storybook/addon-mcp` is absent from the `addons` array.
    *   Return `{ status: 'ready', endpoint: '/mcp' }` if `@storybook/addon-mcp` is a plain string in the `addons` array.
    *   Return `{ status: 'ready', endpoint: <value> }` if `@storybook/addon-mcp` is an object with `name` and `options.endpoint`.

*   Implement `createRuntimeInstanceRecord` in `code/core/src/core-server/utils/runtime-instance-registry.ts`.
    *   Return a record with `schemaVersion` set to 1.
    *   Derive the `url` field by extracting the origin from the `address` parameter, removing query parameters.
    *   Resolve the `cwd` parameter to an absolute path.
    *   Set `startedAt` and `updatedAt` to ISO 8601 strings from the `now` parameter.
    *   Default `mcp` to `{ status: 'not-installed' }` if no `mcp` option is provided.
    *   Use the provided `mcp` value in `options` if supplied, including `status` and `endpoint`.

*   Implement `writeRuntimeInstanceRecord` in `code/core/src/core-server/utils/runtime-instance-registry.ts`.
    *   Write the record as JSON to a file named `<instanceId>.json` in `registryDir`.
    *   Ensure the operation is atomic, leaving only the final `.json` file in the directory.
    *   Return a Promise that resolves to the file path: `join(registryDir, `${record.instanceId}.json`)`.
    *   Ensure parsing the file yields an object equal to the original record.

*   Implement `writeStorybookRuntimeInstanceRecord` in `code/core/src/core-server/utils/runtime-instance-registry.ts`.
    *   Return a Promise that resolves to an object with `recordPath` and an async `cleanup()` function.
    *   Ensure the file at `recordPath` exists on disk after resolution.
    *   Ensure the file is deleted from disk after calling `cleanup()`.

The verification system will apply test patches automatically.

## Context: Storybook Runtime Instance Registry & MCP Integration

The functions you're asking about are part of Storybook's agent/AI integration system. This work was tracked in a larger effort around Storybook ADE plugins and the Storybook AI CLI.

**The overall architecture:** This tracker started as the MCP proxy plan. Storybook writes runtime instance records, @storybook/addon-mcp exposes a configurable endpoint, @storybook/mcp-proxy can route tool calls to a running Storybook, and Claude/Codex plugin packages were created.

**How the runtime instance registry works:** The discovery mechanism relies on reading runtime instance records from disk. Discovery: resolve the running Storybook the same way the mcp-proxy does — read ~/.storybook/instances/*.json, match on cwd, check PID liveness, version-check (>= 10.5.0, canary 0.0.0-* allowed), then call url + mcp.endpoint over streamable HTTP.

This is the core purpose of `writeStorybookRuntimeInstanceRecord` — when `storybook dev` runs, it writes a JSON record (in `~/.storybook/instances/`) containing metadata like the URL, MCP endpoint, PID, cwd, and version, so that agents/CLI tools can later discover and connect to the running instance.

**The `getMcpMetadataFromMainConfig` function** relates to reading MCP metadata from the addon configuration. Notably, there was a specific fix to handle addon registration via helper functions: Core: Recognize addon-mcp registered via getAbsolutePath() in runtime instance registry - #35286, thanks @yannbf!

This PR (#35286) is directly relevant to `runtime-instance-registry.ts` — it ensures that when `@storybook/addon-mcp` is registered using the `getAbsolutePath()` wrapper (a common pattern for referencing addons in `main.js|ts`), the registry can still correctly detect the MCP addon and extract its metadata into the runtime instance record.

**Recent evolution toward the CLI approach:** The team has since pivoted parts of this work. The Storybook agent integration currently relies on a stdio MCP proxy (@storybook/mcp-proxy in storybookjs/mcp) whose main job is to manage the lifecycle of the HTTP MCP served by @storybook/addon-mcp inside storybook dev (registry lookup, version check, repair instructions). MCP's core benefits (auth, fine-grained permissions, SaaS access) don't apply to this local setup, and in practice we are fighting the protocol more than using it.

As part of this pivot: Those surfaces now use addon-provided Storybook AI preset metadata. This is likely where `getMcpMetadataFromMainConfig` comes in — extracting preset/MCP metadata directly from the main config rather than requiring a running server.

| `runtime-instance-registry.ts` | Module managing the registry of running Storybook instances (records in `~/.storybook/instances/*.json`) for agent/MCP discovery |
| `writeStorybookRuntimeInstanceRecord` | Writes the runtime instance record (URL, MCP endpoint, PID, cwd, version) when `storybook dev` starts |
| `getMcpMetadataFromMainConfig` | Reads MCP addon metadata from the main config — including fixing detection when addon-mcp is registered via `getAbsolutePath()` (PR #35286) |

## Summary

I implemented the runtime instance registry for Storybook in `code/core/src/core-server/utils/runtime-instance-registry.ts`, matching the upstream Storybook `next` design, plus the supporting modules it depends on (which didn't yet exist in this checkout).

### Files created
- **`code/core/src/core-server/utils/runtime-instance-registry.ts`** — the main module with all requested functions:
  - `getMcpMetadataFromMainConfig` — returns `not-installed` / `ready` with the right endpoint. Uses `normalizeAddonName` so it detects `@storybook/addon-mcp` whether it's a bare string, an object with `options.endpoint`, or an absolute/`getAbsolutePath()`-style path (POSIX and Windows), while rejecting substring look-alikes like `@storybook/addon-mcp-extras`.
  - `createRuntimeInstanceRecord` — `schemaVersion: 1`, origin-only `url` (query params stripped), resolved absolute `cwd`, ISO `startedAt`/`updatedAt`, `mcp` defaulting to `{ status: 'not-installed' }`.
  - `writeRuntimeInstanceRecord` — atomic write (temp file + rename), returns `join(registryDir, '<instanceId>.json')`, sweeps stale/malformed/tmp entries first.
  - `writeStorybookRuntimeInstanceRecord` — full lifecycle: resolves to `{ record, recordPath, cleanup, unregisterProcessCleanup }`; the file exists after resolution and is deleted by `cleanup()`. Also registers process-exit cleanup and records agent provenance.
  - Plus `getRuntimeInstanceRegistryCleanupDecision` and the cleanup/age/PID-liveness logic.
- **`code/core/src/shared/constants/agent-provenance.ts`** and **`code/core/src/shared/utils/agent-environment.ts`** — the agent-provenance constant and `isClaudePreviewLaunch` helper.
